# `react/no-nested-components`

**Components are not defined inside other components**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-react` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-react` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:react/recommended` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (moving the component out means passing in the values it closed over as props) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-react-hooks/static-components`, `@eslint-react/no-nested-component-definitions` |

## What it checks

A PascalCase function that renders JSX is not defined inside another component — a function
component, or a class component's `render()`. Lower-case helpers that return JSX
(`const renderRow = () => <tr />`) are not components and are fine.

**Why:** A component defined during render is a new component type on every render: React unmounts the old one and mounts the new one, so its state and its DOM are thrown away each time.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-react
pip install codelaw-rules-react
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:react/recommended` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:react/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"react/no-nested-components" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "react/no-nested-components" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"react/no-nested-components" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"react/no-nested-components" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"react/no-nested-components" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "react/no-nested-components": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore react/no-nested-components: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore react/no-nested-components expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule react/no-nested-components --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain react/no-nested-components       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule react/no-nested-components  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>              # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Move the component to the top level of the module.
2. Pass the values it read from the outer component as props.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
function List({ items }) {
  const Item = ({ text }) => <li>{text}</li>;
  return <ul>{items.map((t) => <Item key={t} text={t} />)}</ul>;
}
```

#### Do

```js
const Item = ({ text }) => <li>{text}</li>;

function List({ items }) {
  return <ul>{items.map((t) => <Item key={t} text={t} />)}</ul>;
}
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
function List({ items }) {
  function Item({ text }) {
    return <li>{text}</li>;
  }
  return <ul>{items.map((t) => <Item key={t} text={t} />)}</ul>;
}
```

#### Do

```jsx
function Item({ text }) {
  return <li>{text}</li>;
}

function List({ items }) {
  return <ul>{items.map((t) => <Item key={t} text={t} />)}</ul>;
}
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
function List({ items }: { items: string[] }) {
  const Item = ({ text }: { text: string }) => <li>{text}</li>;
  return <ul>{items.map((t) => <Item key={t} text={t} />)}</ul>;
}
```

#### Do

```tsx
const Item = ({ text }: { text: string }) => <li>{text}</li>;

function List({ items }: { items: string[] }) {
  return <ul>{items.map((t) => <Item key={t} text={t} />)}</ul>;
}
```

## Differences from the source

- The React Compiler's `static-components` reports a component made during render only where it is used as JSX; @eslint-react's `no-nested-component-definitions` reports the definition. codelaw reports the definition, like @eslint-react.
- A component made by a call (`const C = styled(…)`, `const C = memo(…)` with no function written there) or passed inline as a JSX prop is not reported.
